#2222. Andoni Iraola: Liverpool cannot ‘sustain the level’ I want

Andoni Iraola has conceded that Liverpool cannot currently “sustain the level” he expects after his side squandered a two-goal lead for the second match in a row.

In the Spaniard’s first game at Anfield since becoming manager, Monaco fought back to win 3-2 by virtue of Paris Brunner’s late glancing header seven days on from Leeds United’s 4-2 victory in Chicago, emphasising Liverpool’s alarming lack of depth, particularly in defence.

“We played a good first half, especially a good 30 minutes. Right now we probably don’t have much more, in terms of the levels required to play like this. They deserved to turn around the game.

“We won the first two pre-season games, but the last two we cannot sustain the level we want for all of the game. As soon as we made some changes, players start to get tired and we cannot sustain that level. So, we have work to do.”

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Alisson, Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo all made their first appearances and contributed to a lively first-half in which Iraola’s commitment to man-to-man marking and an intensive pressing structure were evident out of possession. With the ball in the first half they demonstrated the kind of slick passing that Bournemouth employed to carve opponents open on the counter-attack.

A nimble one-two between Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai allowed the Dutch midfielder to set up Alexander Isak to score with a shot from 16 yards and the most expensive player in English football history laid claim to the second, too, when he seemed to hook in a rebound from Lukas Hradecky’s save while lying in the six-yard box.

Later he would graciously acknowledge that he and Florian Wirtz had connected with the ball simultaneously and he was happy to yield the credit to his team-mate.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

At that point it seemed that victory would be a cakewalk but just before half-time Aleksandr Golovin caught Van Dijk out with a feint and late swerve to the right, tripping over the Liverpool captain’s clumsy hack. Despite a heavy limp, Golovin hammered the penalty past Alisson’s dive to make it 2-1 at the break.

Iraola rationed his early changes at the start of the second half to two but Liverpool could not regain their rhythm and Mika Biereth capitalised on a Gravenberch error to score the equaliser after battling to be first to the rebound when Giorgi Mamardashvili saved his first effort, stroking his effort through Wataru Endo’s legs.

Cue five substitutions as soon as that goal had gone in and a raft more followed, killing the remaining half-hour of all momentum and cohesion. By the time Brunner exploited a dozy mix-up between Milos Kerkez and Federico Chiesa about whose responsibility he was at a corner to flash his header past Mamardashvili, only two of the 22 starters were still on the pitch.

Liverpool: Alisson (Mamardashvili 46), Tsimikas (Kerkez 59), Van Dijk (c) (Chambers 59), Ndukwe (Endo 46), Frimpong (Ramsay 75), Gravenberch (Nyoni 59), Gakpo (Ngumoha 59), Wirtz (McConnell 59), Koumas (Chiesa 75), Isak (Muñoz 59)Substitutes: Morrison, Davies.Goals: Isak (16), Wirtz (29)Monaco: Hradecky, Nazinho (Mawissa 75), Dier (c) (Kehrer 75), S Sané, Vanderson (Teze 46), Golovin (Idumbo 75), Cabral (Soubeir 75), Camara (Benzahra 64), Detourbet (Coulibaly 64), Biereth (Brunner 80), Abline (Konaté 64).Substitutes: Assab, Kohn, Lienard, Nibombe, Touré.  Goals: Golovin (44 pen), Biereth (56), Brunner (88)

They played well in the first half, as they did against Leeds, but lost all shape and structure in the second half to lose 3-2.

Yellow card for Konate for clattering into Endo late. That’s the last of the action.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 3 (Brunner)  Brilliant near-post glancing header from a devilishly whippy, dipping corner. Kerkez doing his best Rip van Winkle impression.

Diligent defensive work by Ngumoha stops Konate’s run down the outside left.

A final substitution, hopefully. Brunner replaces Biereth. Konate’s shot, a pearoller, is easily saved by Mamardashvili after A mix-up between Kerkez and Munoz.

As usual, the substitutions have killed the game. Watched Leeds vs RB Leipzig yesterday. They played two 60 minute matches which kept it more competitive for longer but still descended into a kickabout late on.

Mawissa, Kehrer, Idumbo and Soubeir have replaced Nazinho, Dier, Golovin and Cabral.

Monaco also made changes, four I think. Will catch up with then once they’re confirmed. Ramsey is into the game straight away tp stop Coulibaly’s shot.

Ramsay, Chiesa and Elliott are coming on for Szoboszlai, Frimpong and Koumas. Lovely applause for Elliott.

Konate sweeps a left-foot shot from the left of the box past the right post with Mamardashvili forced into a headlong dive. Liverpool have lost their defensive shape and intensity, allowing Monaco to punch holes through the lines with some direct running.

Nazinho gets round Frimpong down the Monaco left and cuts back the perfect pass to put it on a plate for Coulibaly who hammers a left-foot shot from the right of the D that Mamardashvili throws up his hands to block. That would have stung. Good save. A flag would have meant it wouldn’t have counted but even so Frimpong’s defensive work wasn’t good enough.

It’s been very scrappy since the changes but then Ngumoha pounces on to a loose ball, glides up the right and tries to play Koumas in behind the back four. Sadly, he overhits the pass which trickles out for a goal-kick. Cue an ovation and cries of ‘Rio! Rio!’

Three changes for Monaco with Detoubet, Abline and Camara departing for Benzhara, Coulibaly and Konaté.

Ngumoha has gone to the right wing and Koumas is playing through the middle as a false nine.

Liverpool make five changes with Gakpo, Van Dijk, Wirtz, Tsimikas and Isak departing while Munoz makes his ‘debut’ with Ngumoha, Nyoni, Chambers, McConell and Kerkez.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 2 (Biereth) Mistake by Gravenberch allows Golovin to play a pass into the left half of the box for Biereth. His first shot is well saved by Mamardashvili at full stretch but his tenacity allowed him to get to the rebound ahead of Endo, swivel and stick his second effort in to equalise.

Monaco overplay at the edge of the box, Detourbet, Biereth and Abline playing ‘after you. Claud’, instead of shooting.

A slick, short passing move between Gravenberch, Wirtz and Isak ends with Isak on the deck in the box after Gravenberch’s step-over allowed the ball to run to him. Isak took a touch to move the ball on to his left but gave the defender a glimmer of it and he hacked it away before felling Isak as well as collateral damage.

Quiet start to the half. Biereth just pressed Mamardashvili but the keeper managed to sweep the ball away even though under more pressure than he would have expected.

Liverpool try to play out from the back with Mamardashvili spearing a straight pass to Gravenberch who tried to knock it round the corner for Endo but the ball skidded under his studs and out for a throw-in.

Isak is apparently claiming both goals. Replays are indistinct. He could have clipped it in off his heel as he had a swing at the ball while grounded at the same time as Wirtz.

Our second goal of the game, scored by Wirtz… we think 🤔 pic.twitter.com/FUzA363Oxw

Endo has slotted in at centre-back alongside Van Dijk.

Half-time changes: Mamardashvili for Alisson and Endo for Ndukwe.

For Monaco, Teze for Vanderson at right-back.

Much to admire in that first-half performance from Liverpool’s front six and centre-backs, the latter two particularly out of possession and winning it back. The man-to-man system is working well for them. But they should be out of sight by now instead of leading by only a goal.

Liverpool free-kick on the right after a foul on Koumas. Szoboszlai whips in the cross and Van Dijk gets up first to the left of the penalty spot but bludgeons his header about a foot wide of the right post.

Charlie Adam says the penalty was ‘a soft one’ but Van Dijk did not adjust when Golovin shifted it to his right, stuck out a leg and Golovim understandably decided to topple over the hurdle.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 1 (Golovin, pen) Speared it into the top right. Alisson went the right way but was beaten for pace and power.

The referee, Jarred Gillett, gives Monaco a penalty. It was deserved, too. Golovin went on a driving run down the middle, shifted it to his right and was tripped by Van Dijk.

Liverpool are well worth their lead. They are streets ahead of Monaco.

A microcosm of the game so far: Liverpool pass goes astray, a player wins it back – this time Gakpo – by snapping into a tackle before laying it off to his left for the unmarked Tsimikas to skim a low shot about a foot wide of the left post from 25 yards.

Monaco have done very little since that wee salvo in the opening minute but just now Abline was given too much space from distance but whacked his shot into the Kop.

Big cheer from the crowd for Hugo Ekitike

The impressive Koumas diddles Nazinho with a Cruyff turn but then thumps his shot straight into Hradecky’s chest.

Liverpool 2 Monaco 0 (Wirtz) Pass chipped out to Koumas down the right who arcs a cross to the back post. Gakpo meets it with a header back across goal to Isak whose first effort from a couple of yards is blocked but the ball gets stuck under Isak’s falling body and Wirtz is Johnny on the Spot to stab it in from a 18 inches as Dier tried to scramble it away.

Liverpool have been impressive so far but if there has been a weakness it’s still the balance in central midfield defensively. Going forward both Gravenberch and Szobiszlai have dovetailed together well. They win the ball back when Van Dijk steps out and the midfield two fly forward to tee up Koumas for a shot that strikes Dier.

Chance for Wirtz, who opens his body from the left of the D to try to bend a shot into the bottom right corner but fizzes it the wrong side of the post.

It’s been pretty breathless since the goal, Liverpool dozily letting Monaco through the middle before twice cutting Monaco apart in midfield only for Isak to overrun a pass in the box delivered by Wirtz and then Koumas to shoot over.

Liverpool 1 Monaco 0 (Isak) Chip to Gakpo down the left of the box, he clips it first time back to Gravenberch in the D who lays it off to Szoboszlai. Ping-ping-ping. Szoboszlai keeps the tempo high with return, the one in the one-two with Gravenberch who picks out Isak to bury a shot from about 15 yards into the bottom left corner.

Alex on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/PT6AYrLxyz

Excellent move from Liverpool, instigated by Ndukwe’s fine tackle on Biereth. He knocks it short to Gravenberch who arrows a 60-yard pass out to Koumas hurtling down the right. He measures his cross perfectly for Gakpo stealing in off the left wing and though he connects powerfully with the meat of his brow, he bashes it straight at the keeper. He was offside in any case, it transpires.

Charlie Adam on co-comms points out that Liverpool are going man-to-man now in classic Iraola/Bielsa style and when the camera goes high you can see it, especially with the full-backs.

Liverpool are carving the middle of the park up with incisive passing. Szoboszlai starts a move that sends Isak down the left of the box. He traps the chip, turns back to face away from goal and taps a pass back to Wirtz who gallops on to it and bends a shot that Hradecky dives low to his left to beat away with a firm left wrist. Frimpong pounces on the rebound and clips a tame effort straight at Hradecky who had quickly restored himself to the vertical.

Van Dijk gobbles up a long pass over Ndukwe, snuffing out any possibility of Biereth getting there first.

Tsimikas is free down the left but overhits his cross on the run when Isak was begging for a cut-back. The left-back went for the back post and ballooned his centre behind, miles beyond Koumas and Wirtz.

Liverpool defend the corner solidly and Frimpong races away on the counter, bombing on to the ball and sprinting into the Monaco half. But his touch is not as sound as his pace and Monaco deal with him when he fluffs his control.

A period of applause in memory of Kevin Keegan ❤️ pic.twitter.com/AkPZG7babe

Liverpool kick off defending the Kop. They roll the ball back to Frimpong who chips a long pass up the right to Koumas who hares on to the pass down the right and crosses, just beyond Isak. Hradecky gathers and bowls the ball out. A mistake by Tisimikas lets Biereth barrel through the inside-right to hammer a shot that Alisson turns behind for a corner.

The crowd applauds in the modern way. My goodness he was a terrific player. Saw him play for Liverpool, Southampton and Newcastle. Absolutely relentless.

Virgil van Dijk has the pennant. Liverpool are wearing all red with the paint splashes of the 1990 kit. Monaco are in a very pale green.

For me it’s a special game, most of the players and people will be ‘it’s [just] a pre-season friendly’, but for me it’s a lot more than this. It will be the first time I have the chance to go out, to feel this stadium and I hope we can also perform well.

It’s a good game for us, because it’s going to be demanding, it’s a team that wants to dominate and they also want to press high so we will see how we are.

I think the cases of Ali[sson], Cody, and Virgil I think it’s their first game. It shouldn’t go longer than 45 minutes, maybe a little bit more if they feel comfortable.

Also for some of the others Ryan, Flo, and Alex, it’s the second game so we have to be aware of those things.

But the league starts in two weeks, so we cannot wait also too much; we have to give them quality minutes.

I think today is going to be a good reference, two games – Monaco and Como – teams that try dominate the game, they are very good in possession, so they will demand us the best without the ball. If we want to control the game and also physical teams, they are probably a very good test.

I hope we are at the level and we can do very good games.

Liverpool Alisson; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Van Dijk, Tsimikas; Szoboszlai, Gakpo; Koumaz, Wirtz, Gakpo; Isak.

Monaco Hradecky; Vanderson, Dier, Sané, Nazinho; Detourbet, Cabral, Camara, Golovin, Abline, Biereth.

Le 𝐗𝐈 qui débutera cette rencontre face à 𝐋𝐢𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐨𝐥 📋 pic.twitter.com/2cOYRbzUEN

🥳 Feliz aniversário, 𝐅𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐩𝐞 𝐋𝐮𝐢́𝐬! 🎉Notre coach fête aujourd'hui ses 41 ans 🎂 pic.twitter.com/VTd4BQ5rRK

Alisson, Van Dijk and Gakpo return, Ndukwe continues in defence.

The Reds to take on AS Monaco at Anfield!Watch the match LIVE on All Red Video 📺

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the first of two Liverpool home friendlies after their preseason tour of the United States. Andoni Iraola’s side saw off Wrexham and Sunderland in their first two matches but gave away a two-goal lead at half-time in the final fixture and ended up being beaten 4-2 by Leeds United in Chicago in the last game after multiple changes. What did we learn? Not a huge amount in the absence of Virgil van Dijk, Alisson, Víctor Muñoz, Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister, the first four of whom are available today other than an ongoing vulnerability from set-pieces and Curtis Jones looking like he is in desperate need of a fresh start.

This afternoon at Anfield they take on AS Monaco who finished seventh in Ligue 1 this season but are under new management with the recruitment of the former Chelsea and Atlético left-back Filipe Luís as head coach. It’s quite the coup for Le Rocher given he led Flamengo to their first Brazilian title in five years, the Copa Libertadores and the Copa do Brasil in his 18 months in charge.

In pre-season so far he has overseen a 5-2 win over fourth-tier AS Saint-Priest, a 2-0 defeat by Sporting Clube, a 2-2 draw with Cercle Bruges and a 1-0 victory over Getafe. They have sold their best player, Maghnes Akliouche, to PSG for £43m and Aladji Bamba to Newcastle for £34m but have so far retained Mamadou Coulibaly and Folarin Balogun, signed and made Ansu Fati’s loan move into a long-term deal.

Iraola may well persevere with Trey Nyoni in midfield who, after his performances on tour, ought to be on the threshold of a breakthrough season and it would be interesting to see him paired with Ryan Gravenberch just behind Dominik Szoboszlai.

Ifeanyi Ndukwe, who played well in America after coming on for the injured Joe Gomez, does not have a UK work permit and will have to go abroad on loan for the season but Jérémy Jacquet, who has yet to feature, was due to have a fitness test this morning and would be a welcome to boost to a squad whose defence still requires significant reinforcements.

#2221. Tuchel pensa solo all'Inghilterra: "Non lascerò il mio incarico prima di Euro 2028"

Thomas Tuchel non ha alcuna intenzione di lasciare la panchina dell'Inghilterra prima della scadenza del suo contratto. Il commissario tecnico tedesco, arrivato nel 2025 per raccogliere l'eredità di Gareth Southgate, ha messo fine alle recenti speculazioni che lo accostavano ad alcuni grandi club europei.

Intervenuto in conferenza stampa, Tuchel è stato netto: "Non esiste alcuna clausola d'uscita e non ho intenzione di andarmene. Ho firmato questo contratto e voglio restare fino all'Europeo. Voglio disputare quel torneo. Abbiamo qualcosa da portare a termine". Le indiscrezioni si erano intensificate nelle ultime settimane anche in seguito alle difficoltà del Manchester United, che ha esonerato Carrick (arriverà Pochettino); Tuchel, però, ha assicurato che non lascerebbe la nazionale neppure di fronte a un'offerta importante.

Pur confermando la volontà di onorare l'impegno con l'Inghilterra, Tuchel non ha escluso un ritorno su una panchina di club dopo Euro 2028. "Sono aperto a tutto", ha spiegato, ammettendo di sentire la mancanza del ritmo del calcio di tutti i giorni: "Mi mancano le 50 partite a stagione", ha confessato, aggiungendo di rimpiangere anche l'adrenalina dei finali di gara e l'atmosfera degli stadi.

Il Corriere dello Sport fa il punto sulle condizioni di Lautaro e Thuram, che lottano per tornare in campo il prima possibile dopo i problemi fisici accusati nei giorni scorsi. Scrive il quotidiano:

"Solo un affaticamento. Ieri Thuram è tornato alla Pinetina e le sue condizioni sono state immediatamente verificate. Il responso è stato positivo, nel senso che è stato confermato il semplice l’affaticamento, escludendo un vero e proprio infortunio. È chiaro però che la situazione vada monitorata. Nei prossimi giorni, insomma, il francese seguirà un programma personalizzato, che gli permetta di smaltire il piccolo guaio e che, allo stesso tempo, gli consenta di mantenere la condizione. Significa che sarà abile e arruolatile per la trasferta con l’Atalanta? È ancora troppo presto per dare una risposta definitiva. Si capirà meglio con il passare dei giorni. Dall’Inter trapela fiducia. Ma tutto dipende da quando Thuram sarà in grado di tornare ad allenarsi in gruppo".

"In parallelo, Chivu attende buone notizie anche da Lautaro. Ieri, la Pinetina ha riaperto i cancelli per tutti i non convocati. C’era anche l’attaccante argentino. Che ha proseguito con il suo lavoro differenziato, svolto comunque sul campo. I nerazzurri si alleneranno anche oggi e domani. Poi scatterà un nuovo rompete le righe per il weekend, con ripresa fissata per lunedì. Ecco la prossima settimana sarà quella determinante per il Toro. Prima tornerà a lavorare a pieno ritmo e più aumenteranno le chances di averlo a disposizione per l’Atalanta. Al momento, in attacco, l’unica certezza è Esposito. Su chi gli giocherà a fianco a Bergamo, invece, resta il punto interrogativo. La speranza di Chivu è di poter contare sia su Thuram sia su Lautaro, in modo da suddividerne l’utilizzo. Accadrà, però, soltanto se non ci saranno margini di rischio".

#2218. Sassuolo, D'Aversa: "Ho viste 3 gare dal vivo: la gara con la Roma dimostra che serve migliorare"

Roberto D'Aversa, nuovo allenatore del Sassuolo, si è presentato ufficialmente questa mattina al Mapei Football Center come tecnico dei neroverdi: "Io ho visto tre partite dal vivo. Contro il Torino la squadra ha fatto una bella gara, è stata brava a portarla a casa. A Bologna avrebbero meritato un risultato pieno, penso che avrebbero meritato di vincere più con il Bologna che con il Torino, poi con la Roma, c'era una squadra strabiliante in questo momento, non era semplice. Mentre le altre gare non destavano segni di preoccupazione, quella con la Roma sì e bisogna lavorare per migliorare".

Quel qualcosa che manca si può trovare con un gioco diverso o lavorando sulla testa? "Bisogna ritrovare chi è fuori, poi uno analizza la squadra con i numeri, sono importanti, e nel momento in cui si arriva in una squadra che in questo momento ci vede come la peggior difesa, è l'aspetto da migliorare, ma non parlo di un solo reparto, parlo della squadra per intero poiché ci sono giocatori che ti portano a fare tanti gol, ci sono giocatori di qualità, ha numeri da questo punto di vista nella media, l'aspetto da migliorare è l'altro. Si migliora nel duello personale, tutto parte dall'aspetto mentale e non dal modulo".

#2216. Napoli, Bianchini: “Nell’ultimo quinquennio abbiamo lavorato per costruire una forte identità di brand”

Tommaso Bianchini, direttore Generale dell’Area Business della SSC Napoli, ha partecipato al panel “Club, non solo Squadre”, nell’ambito dell’edizione 2026 del Social Football Summit, in corso all’Allianz Stadium di Torino. Nel corso del suo intervento, Bianchini ha ripercorso il processo di ideazione e realizzazione del progetto del Centenario: “Nell’ultimo quinquennio abbiamo lavorato per costruire una forte identità di brand e sviluppare relazioni con partner internazionali che hanno riconosciuto in SSC Napoli un canale privilegiato per entrare in contatto con milioni di tifosi e appassionati in tutto il mondo. La sfida per il futuro è accelerare ulteriormente questo percorso attraverso la creazione di una piattaforma di marketing integrata, capace di rafforzare il posizionamento globale del Club e sviluppare nuove forme di collaborazione con i nostri partner”.

#2215. Lazio-Roma, Nord esaurita in poche ore: possibile quota 30mila

Oltre 20mila presenze sono già garantite tra biglietti e pacchetti; la prima prelazione terminerà il 15 novembre.

La Curva Nord è esaurita per Lazio-Roma del 13 dicembre: i circa 7.800 posti sono terminati in poche ore. Tra biglietti acquistati e pacchetti già sottoscritti, sono garantite oltre 20mila presenze biancocelesti. Per il derby il tifo organizzato tornerà all’Olimpico, sospendendo per novanta minuti la contestazione contro Claudio Lotito.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La vendita è partita mercoledì 11 novembre alle ore 10, con una prima finestra riservata agli abbonati della scorsa stagione. La richiesta ha portato rapidamente all’esaurimento dei posti della Nord ed è stata elevata anche negli altri settori.

Le presenze già garantite superano quota 20mila considerando sia i tagliandi venduti sia i pacchetti sottoscritti in precedenza. Le previsioni indicano la possibilità di oltrepassare i 30mila spettatori biancocelesti: si tratta di una stima, non di un dato già raggiunto.

Il ritorno della Curva all’Olimpico è un’eccezione alla linea tenuta nelle precedenti partite casalinghe, segnate dalla protesta e da spalti semivuoti. Dopo mesi di contestazione, la scelta per la sfida alla Roma non modifica la posizione del tifo organizzato nei confronti della società.

La protesta proseguirà, ma durante la partita l’attenzione dei sostenitori sarà rivolta alla squadra di Gennaro Gattuso. La Nord intende sostenere i calciatori in una delle sfide più sentite della stagione. Il derby rappresenterà dunque una pausa nella contestazione a Lotito, limitata ai novanta minuti di gioco.

#2214. Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on Sunday.

The loss to the German side followed a 3-1 defeat by Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin.

Before kick-off, Bruno Guimarães was paraded to the Arsenal faithful after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday.

But enthusiasm about the Brazilian’s arrival was dampened when Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening 10 minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inácio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner.

The Bundesliga side doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

Ten minutes after half-time, Arsenal pulled a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who scored from Christos Tzolis’s cross. However, moments later Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner.

Arsenal kept their hopes alive through a Viktor Gyokeres penalty after Tzolis was brought down, but Dortmund were able to hold on to claim victory. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shoot-out, which Arsenal won 5-4.

Arsenal still have a number of players to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

As well as Guimarães, there was another addition on display at the Emirates: Arsenal have added last year’s title win to the list of honours displayed inside the stadium.

Arsenal play Cesc Fàbregas’s Como on Wednesday, before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly promoted Coventry City.

Arsenal: Kepa (Meslier 46); White (Julienne 78), Mosquera (Ogunnaike 78), Gabriel (Salmon 60), Calafiori (Hincapié 60); Lewis-Skelly (Vieira 78), Havertz (O’Neill 78), Odegaard (Nwaneri 33); Dowman (Ibrahim 78), Gyokeres (Jesus 78), Tzolis (Martinielli 78). Substitutes: Setford, Nelson, Kabia.Booked: Gabriel.Goals: Nwaneri (54), Gyokeres (69 pen).Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson (Yamamoto 91), Inácio (Prates 59), Bensebaini (Reggiani 78), Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha (Guirassy 60), Mane; Karetsas (Chukwuemeka 46), Beier (Sabitzer 59), Silva (Albert 59). Substitutes: Drewes, Lerema, Kabar, Riedl.Goals: Inácio (7), Karetsas (29), Gadou (58).

Nwaneri steps up with the chance to win the shootout and does so with aplomb, sending Meyer the wrong way, and Arsenal win the shootout 5-4.

The former Chelsea man receives some boos as he steps up but calmly slots home to keep Dortmund’s hopes alive.

Meyer goes the right way but there is far too much power on this penalty from Martinelli. Meyer had no chance of saving that one.

We have the first penalty miss of this shootout as Meslier guesses the right way and saves what was a pretty poor penalty from Albert. Advantage Arsenal.

A few stutters in the run-up but Hincapie slots home into the bottom left corner, with Meyer going the wrong way.

He came on right at the end of the game to take a penalty and rewards the decision from his manager to do so as he lifts it over Meslier diving to his left.

Another penalty scored in the left corner. Meyer again guesses the right way but cannot prevent Vieira.

There is a bit of a stutter in the run-up as Reggiani stares down Meslier and sends the Arsenal keeper the wrong way, finding the same corner as Sabitzer and Jesus.

Meyer in the Dortmund goal guesses the right way but Jesus lifts it over him with a quality penalty.

Meslier takes an age to get ready but Sabitzer does not care, sending the Arsenal keeper the wrong way and emphatically finding the left corner.

Right, we are ready for penalties. Dortmund will take first, with Sabitzer to take their opening penalty up against Meslier.

Arsenal have the ball in the net in the final few seconds and think they have a very late equaliser but Martinelli’s effort is ruled out for an offside. Meyer will be a relieved man in the Dortmund goal as he allowed Martinelli’s shot to go through him.

The final whistle is then blown and Dortmund have beaten Arsenal 3-2 to take the Emirates Cup.

It is perhaps not a massive surprise but the game has lost some flow with all the changes both sides have made during this second half.

There is set to be a penalty shootout at the end of this one, no matter what the final result is.

Former Arsenal midfielder Cesc Fabregas is in attendance, with his Como side taking on Arsenal here on Wednesday.

Jude Bellingham is supporting his younger brother Jobe today at the Emirates:

With just under 15 minutes to go at the Emirates, Arsenal are going to make a number of changes. Plenty of youngsters are entering the fray as are a few experienced players like Jesus and Martinelli.

The Swede sends Meyer the wrong way and slots into the bottom right corner. It is now 3-2 and this game is not over with 20 minutes to go.

Tzolis goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area and referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot. He was caught inside the box and there did not appear to be too many complaints from the visitors.

Nwaneri comes close to getting his second goal of the half. Tzolis rolls it across the face of the penalty area to Nwaneri, who hits it first time and forces Meyer into a good save to his right, pushing it onto the post.

In the aftermath of that Dortmund goal, there are a raft of changes for both sides. Arsenal have brought on Salmon and Hincapie for Calafiori and Gabriel.

Dortmund have brought on the experience of the likes of Sabitzer and Guirassy.

Arsenal had some problems from corners the other day against Betis and they concede minutes after getting a goal back. Arsenal fail to deal with a corner from the right and the ball ends up with Gadou at the back post. Gadou takes one touch before finding the net, despite the best efforts of numerous Arsenal defenders on the line.

Should Inacio have gone down? The young Italian is played in behind the Arsenal defence and has Calafiori all over his back. Inacio ends up losing possession on the edge of the Arsenal penalty area but had he gone down Calafiori could have been in trouble.

Mikel Arteta’s side reduce Dortmund’s lead to just the one goal. Tzolis cuts it back from the left side of the box and picks out Nwaneri eight yards out from goal in the centre of the box. Nwaneri makes no mistake, smashing home and Arsenal are back in this game.

That is good defending from Nwaneri. Just as Chukwuemeka was lining up a shot just outside the box, Nwaneri tracks back and steals it off Chukwuemeka.

White is found on the right side of the box but is denied by Meyer in the Dortmund goal. The subsequent corner comes to nothing.

Dortmund are not far off scoring their third a couple of minutes into this second half. The ball is rolled into the feet of Nmecha outside the box. The German midfielder, who scored a stunner for his country against Curacao at the World Cup, nearly picks out the top corner but it goes just over Meslier’s bar.

Dortmund have brought on former Chelsea and Aston Villa man Chukwuemeka on at the break. Arsenal have made an alteration at the break with Meslier replacing Kepa in goal.

During half-time at the Emirates, the official song of the 2026 Fifa World Cup Dai Dai by Shakira and Burna Boy is being belted out over the tannoy. The World Cup final was exactly three weeks ago today, with three of Arsenal’s players in Spain’s winning squad; David Raya, Mikel Merino and Martin Zubimendi.

Konstantinos Karetsas has arrived. 🇬🇷🇬🇷🇬🇷 pic.twitter.com/nI4A7KPT4o

The first half in north London is brought to an end and it is the visitors Borussia Dortmund who lead 2-0 at the break courtesy of goals from Inacio and Karetsas.

Gabriel is into the book. He is in possession but his touch allows the ball to slightly get away from him. He then slides in to try and retain possession and catches Karetsas.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Nmecha eyes up a repeat of Dortmund’s first goal as he tries to find the run of Inacio into the Arsenal box but this time they cannot quite link up.

After Gyokeres was fouled, Arsenal have a free-kick inside the Dortmund half. Tzolis clips it in and picks out Havertz in space inside the Dortmund box but the German is a fair way out from goal and his header is easily saved by Meyer.

Arsenal want a penalty but the appeals are turned down. It all stems from good work defensively from Tzolis, who drives forward from the edge of his own box and then finds Gyokeres out to his left. Tzolis continues his run into the Dortmund half and is found. Tzolis then finds Gyokeres again, who goes down inside the Dortmund penalty area after a challenge from Gadou but the Swedish striker went down far too easily and that is never a penalty.

Dowman does brilliantly down Arsenal’s right to get past Beier but then goes down just before the byline. Referee Chris Kavanagh blows his whistle and Beier cannot believe it. Replays show that Dowman threw himself to the ground and it was a dive.

Tzolis takes the free-kick and delivers it to the far post, where Gabriel meets it but his powerful header goes over the bar. The Brazilian probably should have scored.

Mikel Arteta has made a change as Nwaneri has replaced Odegaard, who has only recently returned to training after the World Cup.

With it being a warm day in north London, we have a water break. Hopefully they do not catch on after the World Cup. Mikel Arteta is looking pretty animated talking to his side.

What a finish that is to put the German side 2-0 up! 18-year-old Karetsas, who has joined Dortmund from Genk this summer, is afforded too much space outside the Arsenal penalty area as he drives towards the box and punishes the hosts for that, curling a sublime shot into the far corner.

Odegaard slides a clever pass into the right channel to pick out the run of Gyokeres towards the Dortmund box. Mane though slides in with a perfectly-timed challenge to take it off Gyokeres. Mane had to time that right with the challenge being right on the edge of his own box.

Arsenal hit the bar. Dowman does well down Arsenal’s right to drive into the Dortmund box and cuts it back to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes a few touches before getting his shot away, which clips the top of the bar.

A dangerous cross from the left comes all the way to Svensson at the back post but he lacked conviction with his header and it goes wide. Perhaps he should be hitting the target.

Down at the other end Arsenal have a headed chance of their own. Havertz clips in a cross from the left and picks out Gyokeres. The Swede is a fair way out from goal and his header goes wide.

Should Havertz have done better with this opportunity? The German is played in down the right channel and has Gyokeres calling for the cross in space in the centre of the box. Havertz tries to find him but Meyer is out to smother it. Had Havertz found Gyokeres, it would likely have been a simple tap-in for the Swede.

Odegaard appears to be through one-on-one but then goes down just outside the Dortmund box. Mane pleads his innocence but referee Chris Kavanagh does not agree, giving a free-kick. If this was a competitive game, Mane would potentially have been sent off.

Gyokeres will take and opts for power over accuracy. It is safe to say his effort is terrible, blazing over the bar and missing the target by some margin.

Calafiori trips Bellingham as Dortmund attempted to counter. If this was a competitive fixture, Calafiori likely would have been booked for that foul.

Bellingham and Havertz are involved in quite the collision. Both players go for the header and Havertz just gets to it first. Havertz is awarded the foul and is ok.

The German side take the lead inside the opening seven minutes. Nmecha slides a lovely pass through the Arsenal defensive line to pick out the run of Inacio into the Arsenal penalty area. It is a clinical finish from Inacio, who slides his effort into the far corner,

Dortmund’s first proper foray forward causes Arsenal issues and Tzolis is forced to put it behind for Dortmund’s first corner of the game. The inswinger though to the front post is poor and Gyokeres easily heads away from danger.

Gyokeres wins Arsenal their first corner of the game out on the right. Odegaard’s delivery into the near post causes problems for Dortmund and forces Dortmund keeper Meyer to tip over his own bar for another Arsenal corner. Meyer this time punches Odegaard’s delivery away and Dortmund clear their lines.

Moments after Bruno Guimaraes’ unveiling, both sides now emerge from the tunnel and we are moments away from kick-off at the Emirates.

Just before the two sides emerge the tunnel, there is a special guest who comes out first in the form of Bruno Guimaraes. Chants of “Bruno! Bruno!” ring around the Emirates as the Arsenal fans get their first glimpse of him in an Arsenal shirt, although the Brazilian is not involved today.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

Reports are that Jobe’s older brother Jude is at the Emirates today, not that Arsenal fans should think that Jude is swapping Real Madrid for the red half of north London.

Arsenal took the Premier League trophy with them to Dublin on Wednesday night and it is on show today at the Emirates. They kick off the defence of their crown on opening night against newly-promoted Coventry is just under two weeks.

Counting down until kick-off ⏰ Make sure you're in your seats by 1.45pm (UK), Gooners - we have a very special guest in store 👀

When Bruno Guimarães signed for Newcastle United from Lyon in January 2022, much was made of the idea that he had rejected Arsenal in favour of a move to St James’ Park. The Brazilian played along with it, posting a video on his social media pages which featured multiple newspaper headlines about Arsenal wanting to buy him.

The Newcastle fans, still delirious about the recent takeover by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, understandably lapped it up. Their dream was to overthrow the established powers in English football, and the capture of Guimarães was regarded as a sign that they were truly ready to challenge teams of Arsenal’s stature and wealth.

Even the lyrics to the midfielder’s chant referred to the north Londoners, as Newcastle fans sang that Guimarães “could have signed for Arsenal” but chose instead to play “in the famous black and white”.

Yesterday Arsenal announced the signing of Brazilian midfielder Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle for £75m on a four-year deal, with the option of a further year. Here is what the Brazilian had to say:

“I feel good, I feel amazing. I am glad for the opportunity. Since the first time I spoke to (Andrea) Berta and Mikel (Arteta) I was excited. I just felt inside of me that I need a new challenge in my life and I think to be an Arsenal player is going to be an exciting challenge in my life.

“I think after playing two World Cups, I am at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this. I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I am in the right place to do it. I am so excited to start. We have tough games to play this season so the squad is going to be very, very important and I am hopeful we can achieve our dreams.”

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Odegaard; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.Substitutes: Meslier, Setford, Hincapie, Jesus, Martinielli, Vieira, Nwaneri, Nelson, Ibrahim, Kabia, Ogunnaike, Julienne, O’Neill, Salmon.

Borussia Dortmund: Meyer; Svensson, Inacio, Bensebaini, Gadou; Bellingham, Nmecha, Mane; Karetsas, Beier, Silva.Substitutes: Drewes, Guirassy, Chukwuemeka, Sabitzer, Lerema, Prates, Albert, Kabar, Yamamoto, Reggiani, Riedl.

INS:Illan Meslier from Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis from Club Brugge, £34mBruno Guimaraes from Newcastle, £75m

Piero Hincapie’s move from Bayer Leverkusen was made permanent this summer.

OUTS:Leandro Trossard to Besiktas, £18mJakub Kiwior to Porto, £15m

August 1- Girona 1 Arsenal 4August 5-  Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3Today- Arsenal vs Borussia Dortmund (Emirates Cup)August 12- Arsenal vs ComoAugust 16- Arsenal vs Manchester City (Community Shield)

🚨 STARTING XI VS ARSENAL 🚨 pic.twitter.com/Wk6QPOGDnW

🔴 𝗧𝗘𝗔𝗠𝙉𝙀𝙒𝙎 ⚪️🧱 Gabriel at the back©️ Odegaard skippers the side😤 Gyokeres leads the line More pre-season minutes in the tank - let's do this, Gunners ✊🤝 Presented by @deel pic.twitter.com/FQwOjCDAje

Checking in for the Emirates Cup 🛬 pic.twitter.com/mQ1eAESKHY

Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

#2212. Empoli, per Bembnista niente gare con la Polonia U20: è stato fermato da un problema fisico

Il difensore dell’Empoli Dawid Bembnista alla fine non risponderà alla convocazione da parte della Polonia Under 20 per le prossime sfide dell’Under 20 Elite League contro la Germania (venerdì 13 novembre alle ore 20:00 alla Chorten Arena di Białystok) e la Romania (martedì 17 novembre alle ore 19:00 allo Stadion Eugen Popescu di Targoviste).

Come riporta Empolichannel.it il classe 2007, che nelle ultime tre giornate ha trovato sempre più spazio venendo schierato da titolare contro Juve Stabia e Padova, non partirà alla volta della Polonia a causa di un problema fisico, un leggero fastidio al retto addominale che ha fatto propendere sia l’Empoli sia la Polonia per evitare il viaggio e permettergli di proseguire il lavoro con la squadra di Andreoletti e permettergli di recuperare al meglio in vista delle prossime gare.

Restano così tre i giocatori che saranno impegnati in giro per il mondo in questa pausa: Joseph Ceesay, Matteo Egan e Bohdan Popov. Il primo con il Gambia sarà impegnato in due gare contro la Costa d’Avorio valide per le qualificazioni alla Coppa d’Africa, il secondo invece scenderà in campo con l’Irlanda Under 21 nella doppia sfida play off contro la Finlandia che vale l’accesso alla fase finale dell’Europeo di categoria. Mentre il terzo con la sua Ucraina Under 21 giocherà due amichevoli contro Scozia e Stati Uniti.

#2206. Il 12 novembre al Maschio Angioino l’evento «Mezzogiorno, Napoli per l’alternativa» con l’intervento di Nicola Fratoianni

12 NOVEMBRE A NAPOLI L’EVENTO: MEZZOGIORNO, NAPOLI PER L’ALTERNATIVA Sinistra Italiana a Napoli: “Mezzogiorno, Napoli per l’alternativa”. Il 12 novembre al Maschio Angioino il dibattito sul futuro del Sud con Nicola Fratoianni NAPOLI – In un momento storico decisivo per il futuro del Mezzogiorno e del Paese, Sinistra Italiana promuove un appuntamento politico di primario rilievo: l’incontro pubblico dal titolo “Mezzogiorno, Napoli per l’alternativa”, che si terrà giovedì 12 novembre alle ore 17:30 nella prestigiosa cornice della Sala della Loggia presso il Maschio Angioino. L’incontro ha il fine di tracciare una strada chiara per il riscatto sociale ed economico del Sud, mettendo al centro le battaglie storiche per il lavoro, la giustizia sociale, i diritti ed il contrasto alle diseguaglianze territoriali. L’incontro vedrà la partecipazione delle principali voci delle istituzioni, dell’avvocatura e della politica locale e nazionale: Introduce: Gianluca Daniele (già Consigliere Regionale). Presiede: Pietro Rinaldi (R.U. Armena Sviluppo e Responsabile Enti Locali AVS). Modera: Ilaria Urbani (Giornalista de La Repubblica). Interventi programmati: Stefano Loffredo – Segretario Provinciale della Federazione di Napoli di Sinistra Italiana Toti Lange – Consigliere Comunale Annalisa Senese – Avvocata penalista Daniele Cutolo – Presidente Merqurio e avvocato Peppe De Cristofaro – Capogruppo AVS al Senato. Le conclusioni saranno affidate a Nicola Fratoianni, Segretario Nazionale di Sinistra Italiana e Deputato per l’Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra.

#2205. Lazio, derby da record: incasso stimato vicino ai 4 milioni

La previsione supera i tre milioni incassati contro il Bayern nel 2024; gli abbonati sono 4.200.

La Lazio potrebbe incassare circa 4 milioni di euro dalla vendita dei biglietti per il derby con la Roma di domenica 13 dicembre, in programma alle 12.30. Secondo quanto riportato da Il Messaggero, La stima, riportata da Il Messaggero, collocherebbe la partita al primo posto nella storia degli incassi al botteghino del club. La cifra potrebbe essere anche leggermente superiore.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La previsione è legata alla presenza di appena 4.200 abbonati: per questa gara, gran parte delle presenze sugli spalti si tradurrebbe quindi in biglietti acquistati. La società, da anni, non diffonde i dati relativi agli incassi al botteghino.

Il confronto più recente è con il derby del 21 settembre 2025, quando la Lazio incassò 2,2 milioni di euro. In quell’occasione, però, gli abbonati erano quasi trentamila. Per la prossima sfida con la Roma, la stima si avvicina invece ai quattro milioni.

Un incasso di quell’entità supererebbe nettamente i 3 milioni di euro registrati il 14 febbraio 2024, nella gara di andata degli ottavi di Champions League contro il Bayern. Quella sera la Lazio allenata da Sarri vinse 1-0.

La partita con il Bayern aveva già prodotto un incasso superiore di quasi un milione rispetto al debutto nella stessa competizione contro l’Atletico Madrid, il 19 settembre 2023. La sfida terminò in pareggio grazie al gol del portiere Provedel.

#2204. Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

Newcastle’s raft of half-time changes helped David Moyes’s team strengthen their grip further, with Tyrique George adding a stylish third and 19-year-old Harrison Armstrong providing his second assist of the game.

Among the Newcastle players introduced at half-time was 18-year-old Sean Steur, the exciting midfield prospect signed from Ajax this summer. Aladji Bamba and Bazoumana Toure also flickered with promise, but a sharp start from Jaissle’s team faded.

They pulled a goal back late on when Jacob Murphy’s cross found Harvey Barnes at the back post, but they offered little as an attacking force throughout the second half.

Newcastle have two more friendlies, against Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg, before they begin their Premier League season at home to Liverpool.

The club are reeling from the summer departures of Bruno Guimaraes, Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and manager Eddie Howe, but David Hopkinson, the chief executive, struck a bullish tone when he spoke of this being the start of “Newcastle 2.0”.

Everton look the more settled side and club, and the performances of new arrivals Hackney and George were encouraging, while Thierno Barry was sharp in the centre-forward position that has proved so difficult for the club to fill in recent seasons.

Everton kick-off their new season at home to Crystal Palace, and keeping Ndiaye at the club beyond the end of the transfer window will be a priority.

The scoreline is a fair reflection of the game. Everton looked sharper, as well as fitter, and there are more positives for them to take. They look ready for the new season, Newcastle need reinforcements.

Alcaraz bends a shot not far wide from 25 yards for Everton. The game is meandering towards its conclusion now.

Willock collects the ball between the lines, feeds Murphy wide right, and his ball across goal is turned in at the back post by Harvey Barnes.

Moyes makes another pair of changes: Keane and Hackney off, O’Brien and Foster on.

Everton fans are enjoying themselves now, belting out Spirit of the Blues at Murrayfield.

More defending for Newcastle to do but they deal with Hackney’s corner delivery. All too easy for Everton to slice through their midfield in the build up though.

That goal had been coming, and Tyrique George is heavily involved again. He carries the ball forward and finds Armstrong, who returns the favour. George shoots on the swivel and picks out the bottom corner.

If I were a Newcastle fan in the stands, Edinbugh’s city centre hostelries would be looking very alluring just about now. There is not much for them to watch in this season half, they are chasing shadows. Some of that can be put down to the handful of young plyers in their second-half XI.

Tyler Dribbling drops a shoulder down the right, and wins a corner off Harvey Barnes. Everton are finishing this game the stronger, there are more goals in this should they put their foot on the pedal.

Newcastle, with some youngsters in their defence, looking a little ragged against Everton’s direct attacks now, but George runs into traffic at the edge of the box. Then Alcaraz is booked for a cynical foul.

Three more Everton changes on the way: Beto, Dibling and Alcaraz on for Barry, Ndiaye and Dewsbury-Hall.

Hayden Hackney plays a one-two with Tyrique George for Everton, with the former Chelsea winger backheeling the ball into Hackney’s path, and there were unheeded calls for a penalty. It was more of a penalty than the one Everton were awarded in the first half, Lewis Miley tripped him.

Thierno Barry’s performance has been a positive for Everton, could he nail down the No 9 role this season? It has been a problem position for several seasons now. Barry is tripped and Everton have a free-kick.

Dewsbury-Hall almost sneaks a shot in at the near post, but Hornicek tips the ball around the post.

Joe Willock with what was very nearly an exquisite disguised pass, but the flag was up for offside against Jacob Murphy.

Then an amusing moment: great cheers from the crowd as David Moyes heads a Hornicek clearance back down the line. He didn’t fancy the cushioned first touch off his instep, then.

Everton have played some quick one and two-touch football around the box in this game, and another move ends with George shooting over the bar. Everton are making their first change: Patterson off, replaced by Rohl.

The game is still finding its shape again after all those Newcastle changes, but Murphy did force a sharp save from Travers with a low shot from a tight angle.

He keeps to his word from before the game; Hornicek is the only player still on the pitch.

The players on for Newcastle are: Woltemade, Murphy, Willock, Barnes, Ramsey, Johnson, Steur, Pivas, Miley and Charlton.

It looks like an unchanged team from David Moyes, so Everton have a significantly more mature team on the pitch now.

Newcastle made a bright start, but as the half progressed there is no doubt that Everton have been the more dangerous attacking force and the scoreline reflects that. Here come the changes...

Everton have a late corner to defend, after another burst forward from Newcastle’s left-winger Toure. Newcastle try one off the training ground but the ball is cleared.

Thierno Barry almost finds the run of Hackney into the Newcastle penalty, and after a sluggish start, Everton have played some slick football in the attacking third.

A sign of some Newcastle frustration there was Wissa kicks Tyrique George across the shins. A bit naughty that, may even have been worthy of VAR attention in a Premier League game.

The Senegalese sends Hornicek the wrong way and finds the corner. No chance it was a penalty in the first place though, thankfully this is not a competitive game.

This is very soft, there was not much of a challenge by Joelinton on Dewsbury-Hall, but the Everton midfielder goes down in the box and is awarded the penalty.

It really should be 2-0 to Everton, a high-class moving down their left with Armstrong dinking a pass to Barry. He squared to Ndiaye who was free as a bird in the middle, but his shot was too close to Hornicek.

Joelinton runs down a blind alley before lumping a pass out for an Everton throw, and then the Newcastle man fouls Barry. The big Brazilian still finding his legs and getting up to speed.

A moment to forget for both Newcastle centre-backs. Thiaw was bumped and unbalance by Barry, before Botman steps out of defence and kicks fresh air against the Everton forward. Great recovery from Lewis Hall, but the ball breaks for Armstrong, who feeds Barry and he finishes across Hornicek.

Ndiaye has had a quiet start to the game for Everton, but his jinking qualities were on display there to beat a couple of Newcastle defenders. Everton lose the ball in midfield, and Tarkowski makes a superb last-ditch tackle to deny Osula.

Half-hearted appeals for a penalty from Wissa, but Hayden Hackney did not do much wrong. Looks like we will be spared a first-half hydration break, despite it being a sultry evening.

Osula skips through a couple of challenges at the edge of the area but fails to pick a pass in the box. Bazoumana Touré has looked lively for Newcastle on their left flank, and Bamba has done well for them in midfield.

Everton shake themselves into life as an attacking force. Cracking cross from Patterson into the box and Dewsbury-Hall’s run had gone untracked, but he was just stretching and could not generate enough power to beat Hornicek.

Good save from Travers to deny Elanga, but it was Mykolenko who made a hash of things in the box. The left back simply fell over the ball under no pressure. Newcastle the sharper of the two teams so far.

Joelinton feeds Bamba down the left wing for Newcastle who delivers a cross into the penalty area. Keane can only direct his defensive header back towards the penalty spot, but Wissa volleyed over with a first-time hit. Decent chance.

Thierno Barry makes it stick and proves a strong outlet for Everton. Botman brings him down at the expense of a free-kick just beyond the halfway line. Then Wissa drives into the penalty area for Newcastle after a one-two but he fouls Patterson.

Newcastle, playing in their lilac away kit, are the team trying to take the initiative with the ball, but Everton are quite happy staying compact and absorbing pressure. Elanga’s corner delivery is promising, but Osula does not connect cleanly at the back post.

Newcastle’s defenders enjoying comfortable possession in the early stages, Everton sitting off in their 4-4-2 defensive shape.

Wissa peels behind Everton’s defence inside the opening 90 seconds but he cannot lift the ball over Travers.

Bagpipes greet the players at Murrayfield, where the pitch has been reconfigured for football. There are only fans in the lower tier, and still plenty of empty seats even so.

We know it is a time in the pre-season when the legs are not that fresh, we train very intense but we want to play with an idea of how we want to play football. Intense with a vertical approach for sure, everyone gets 45 minutes except the goalkeeper.

Big Dunc and Moyes catch up pre-match! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/Jh4APHOZvX

A word that keeps being used about Jaissle is “special”. Newcastle’s hierarchy believe they have secured the services of a manager who will soon be recognised in the elite tier of European managers. We shall see how this view of the 38-year-old survives contact with a brutal and relentless Premier League campaign.

Newcastle XI: Hornicek; Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; Joelinton, Bamba; Elanga, Wissa, Toure; Osula

Newcastle subs: Gillespie, Harris, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, M Miley, Finneran, Ramsey, Steur, Willock, J Murphy, Barnes, Neave, Woltemade

Your Mags at Murrayfield! ✊ pic.twitter.com/rDXpn0MqCg

Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

“It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle said.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about new signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

“The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”

#2203. Under 21, Baldini annuncia la formazione e difende Camarda: "Sarà il nostro centravanti a lungo"

Silvio Baldini, tecnico dell'Under 21, ha parlato in conferenza stampa alla vigilia della sfida contro la Francia, in amichevole: "Intanto penso che la cosa che vi interessa di più sia sapere chi partirà dall'inizio. Non c'è problema, lo sanno già loro. Ve lo dico: Palmisani, Manè, Comuzzo, Chiarodia, Bartesaghi, Amatucci, Lipani, Dagasso, Cacciamani, Fini e Camarda. Questi sono i primi 11 che partiranno. Si sono allenati tutti bene; come ho detto ai ragazzi, abbiamo due partite molto ravvicinate e poco tempo per recuperare, quindi valuterò se fare tante sostituzioni durante la partita o lasciare un blocco e giocarne un altro lunedì, questo lo deciderò in base alla gara di domani.

Come sempre, qui è come ritrovarsi in una famiglia. Quando ci sono persone che lavorano all'estero, o che comunque tornano a casa, cosa c'è? C'è una grande festa, una grande armonia. Quando vedo questi ragazzi mi sembra di vivere le emozioni di una grande famiglia; loro sono speciali e quando ci si ritrova qui è bellissimo. Hanno saputo distinguere la professionalità del lavoro dal divertimento: in campo sono persone molto serie che ci tengono a migliorarsi, mentre a tavola la regola numero uno è l'allegria, voglio vederli scherzare e sorridere. Per me sono un dono divino, non esagero, sono speciali.

La Francia è una squadra forte, lo sappiamo, ma a noi non interessa chi andiamo ad affrontare: ci interessa essere liberi mentalmente di giocare la partita come vogliamo. Sappiamo che in entrambe le fasi bisogna essere bravi: quando abbiamo la palla dobbiamo cercare di fare le nostre cose, e se loro sono più bravi a impedirglielo, sappiamo anche soffrire, recuperare e tenere gli spazi stretti. Ripeto, se sono ragazzi speciali è proprio perché riescono a fare tante cose che in pochi giorni non è facile fare".

Hai dovuto fare uno sforzo in più o dire qualche parola a Francesco Camarda, che sta vivendo un periodo un pochino complicato per il suo impiego al Milan? "A Camarda ripeto sempre di togliersi dalla testa tutte le cose negative. Deve pensare che è fortunato, è un ragazzo giovanissimo che gioca in Serie A ed è in Nazionale. È un classe 2008, quindi sarà il centravanti di questa Under 21 anche nel prossimo biennio. Gli dico di giocare a calcio con il gusto di farlo, senza pensare troppo allo spazio o alla mancanza di esso; deve cercarselo in allenamento, divertirsi e poi, insieme alle persone che lo circondano, deciderà cosa fare a gennaio, se cercare più continuità altrove o meno. Quando sono con me questi problemi non esistono, perché prendiamo il calcio come un premio e non solo come sofferenza. I momenti di difficoltà aiutano a diventare ancora più bravi".

In questo anno e mezzo ha lanciato tantissimi giovani: quanto sono importanti per lei e cosa significano? "L'ho sempre detto e lo ripeterò: questi ragazzi sono stati un dono divino. Non credevo potesse nascere un feeling così forte. Parliamo di tante cose che vanno oltre il semplice modulo o la tattica (4-3-3, 4-2-3-1, 3-5-2); mi fanno sentire utile non solo per spiegare la fase difensiva o offensiva, ma per dare spunti affinché diventino persone migliori, e di conseguenza giocatori migliori. Questo mi dà una grande gratificazione".

Si aspettava una crescita così importante da parte di Lulli? "È cresciuto moltissimo nella Roma ed è giusto che i giovani bravi facciano parte dell'Under 21. Non lo conoscevo benissimo prima, sapevo che era uno dei migliori in Primavera. Si è inserito subito nel gruppo alla perfezione, sembrava con noi già da un anno".

Su Ekhator: "Ha grandissime qualità, si sacrifica per la squadra ed è molto maturo per la sua età (ha compiuto 20 anni ieri). Legge le situazioni in campo con grande lucidità: la Juventus si accorgerà di che giocatore ha in casa, ha un grande futuro davanti, è un ragazzo fortissimo".

Lei ha in rosa giocatori con un alto minutaggio nei club e altri che invece giocano meno e stanno in panchina. Nota differenze quando arrivano in Nazionale? Deve gestirli o motivarli in modo diverso? E una battuta su Inacio: come l'ha visto dopo la mancata convocazione o il mancato esordio in Nazionale Maggiore? "Chi gioca di più nel proprio club è certamente più pronto, ha più gamba e gestisce meglio la fatica. Tuttavia, quando arrivano qui sono talmente motivati ed entusiasti che riescono a superare qualsiasi momento di scarso impiego con il club, perché sanno di avere un'opportunità unica per dimostrare il loro valore. Per quanto riguarda Inacio, è un ragazzo molto promettente e di grande qualità che ci darà una mano. Non so i motivi per cui non ha debuttato in Maggiore, ma qui con noi si sta comportando alla grande, ha tanta voglia e in queste due partite avrà sicuramente il suo spazio".

Un acquisto era già ampiamente programmato in estate, ma, se le condizioni lo richiedessero, l'Inter potrebbe anche anticipare a gennaio un colpo in difesa. E, secondo Tuttosport, il ds nerazzurro Baccin avrebbe già un nome sul taccuino:

"Dario Baccin è già al lavoro per rinforzare la rosa dell’Inter per la stagione 2027/28. Nello specifico i nerazzurri interverranno sicuramente in difesa, andando finalmente a completare totalmente un reparto dove da anni si cercano profili veloci, dai piedi educati e anche intercambiabili nel sistema di Chivu. Dopo gli addii di De Vrij e Acerbi è arrivato Stones – su cui a livello tecnico non ci possono essere dubbi -, ma la tenuta fisica dell’inglese, sinora in campo solo 144’ tra campionato e Champions (per un totale di 4 spezzoni) e tornato tra i convocati col Como dopo quasi due mesi di infortunio, impone un certo tipo di riflessioni e azioni".

"In questo senso, se dovessero sorgere nuovi dubbi e perplessità sulle condizioni del giocatore, l’Inter potrebbe anche anticipare un colpo a gennaio, altrimenti si agirà come programmato in estate. Sul taccuino di Baccin, oltre ai già noti Finn Jeltsch, centrale dello Stoccarda - nonché finalista dell’ultima edizione del Golden Boy – e Chris Richards del Crystal Palace -, si è aggiunto anche, secondo Sportitalia, Ignacio Ovando, diciannovenne del Rosario Central, già nei radar della selezione argentina. Il sudamericano piace anche al Napoli, costa 15-20 milioni e di lui in Patria si parla un gran bene".

#2200. Ricordate Sangaré? Meteora alla Roma, a gennaio può andare a giocare a Francoforte

Forse non tutti si ricorderanno di Buba Sangaré (19 anni), potrebbe essere più semplice per i tifosi della Roma, perché il suo percorso nella società giallorossa lo ha visto soltanto scendere in campo con la formazione Primavera senza mai avere l'occasione di vestire la maglia della prima squadra. Una vera e propria meteora giallorossa, l'esterno classe 2007, che però sta trovando gloria in Spagna. E che presto potrebbe anche cambiare casacca per un altro top campionato europeo.

Normale l'affinità con la Spagna: la penisola iberica è stato il terreno in cui Sangaré si è sviluppato come calciatore, nelle giovanili del Levante. Da lì lo ha acquistato la Roma nell'estate del 2024, investendo una cifra comunque non così banale per un giocatore all'epoca neanche maggiorenne e totalmente sconosciuto: 2,2 milioni di euro. Dopo un anno e mezzo di Primavera, è ripartito verso la Spagna a gennaio 2026, trasferendosi in prestito a quell'Elche che ha poi riscattato a titolo definitivo versando 4,5 milioni di euro nelle casse dei capitolini.

Oggi sull'ex Roma si sono posate attenzioni in Bundesliga. C'è l'Eintracht Francoforte, alla ricerca di un nuovo esterno destro, che starebbe studiando la situazione e preparando un futuro assalto. Per un trasferimento che necessiterebbe la doppia cifra di milioni di euro da mettere sul piatto.

Ci sono tanti discorsi in ballo per l'Inter in vista del futuro. Tanti nomi che attendono di prolungare il proprio rapporto per il club. Ma, come vi abbiamo riferito in più occasioni, Oaktree ha cambiato linea: gli stipendi fissi dovranno essere più bassi, parzialmente sostituiti da bonus legati a rendimento, individuali e collettivi. Scrive il Corriere dello Sport:

"Più vinciamo e più ti paghiamo. In stretta sintesi, è questa la linea che l’Inter vuole tenere per i rinnovi di contratto. Sono diversi i discorsi in ballo, a cominciare da Carlos Augusto, passando per Dimarco, Thuram, Akanji, fino ad arrivare a Calhanoglu, in scadenza alla fine della stagione".

"Baccin, una volta divenuto ds in prima persona, ha avviato un giro di consultazioni con i vari rappresentanti dei giocatori interisti. E a tutti è già stato spiegato che l’idea è quella di inserire nei nuovi accordi una quota fissa meno consistente, aggiungendola però ad una quota variabile più ricca e abbondante, legata principalmente ai risultati della squadra".

#2198. Manna a KKN: “Tanti infortuni, ma non devono essere un alibi. Pensiamo di aggregare Neres, Favasuli e Spinazzola da sabato”

Giovanni Manna, direttore sportivo del Napoli, ha parlato a Radio Kiss Kiss Napoli: “Emergenza infortuni? Ci attendono molte gare alla ripresa. Il periodo non è dei più semplici, non abbiamo mai avuto la rosa a disposizione ma questo non deve essere un alibi, anche le altre squadre hanno subìto infortuni. Dobbiamo crescere e lavorare partita dopo partita. Sicuramente ci sono stati degli aspetti sia positivi che negativi. Dopo la vittoria di Monza e la grande prestazione contro la Roma, le sconfitte di Oporto e Torino ci hanno tolto un po’ di certezze. Contro la Lazio è stata una sfida complicata, i biancocelesti hanno giocato più liberi mentalmente, la reazione che abbiamo avuto nel secondo tempo è fortemente incoraggiante. C’è un Napoli ha voglia di uscire da questo momento. Speriamo di dare una linfa nuova alla squadra con la ripresa. Parte della squadra è libera fino a sabato. Abbiamo preferito non spezzettare il periodo di riposo, è stato un periodo molto intenso. Stiamo recuperando dei calciatori. Pensiamo di aggregare Neres, Favasuli e Spinazzola da sabato. Speriamo di accelerare e recuperare gradualmente Badiashile, Di Lorenzo e Alisson sperando di non incorrere in situazioni spiacevoli. Lavoriamo e proviamo a recuperare le energie. Siamo assolutamente consci della situazione, non siamo contenti di questo avvio di stagione. Se abbiamo sbagliato e fatto delle valutazioni non corrette, vogliamo lavorare e risolvere. Abbiamo sempre cercato di onorare la maglia, sono sicuro che usciremo insieme e uniti da questa situazione. Le critiche sono state troppo strumentalizzate. Vogliamo lavorare ed essere uniti, speriamo di fare un filotto di vittorie per i nostri tifosi. Sicuramente le ultime sfide hanno presentato prestazioni di livello. Nella vita, come nel calcio, i dettagli e l’attenzione fanno la differenza. Se non siamo riusciti a recuperare e portare a casa il risultato finale, qualcosa abbiamo sbagliato. Dobbiamo capire dove crescere e ritrovare continuità. Dobbiamo fare meglio e lavorare meglio. Mercato? Con il mister e il presidente ci confrontiamo ogni giorno. In questo momento, qualche precauzione la troviamo sempre. Abbiamo le idee chiare, cercheremo di migliorare la rosa. Dobbiamo però arrivarci a gennaio: ci sono tante partite. Dobbiamo dare continuità di risultati. Lo scorso anno abbiamo speso tanto, forse dovevamo spendere meglio, lo dico anche facendo autocritica. Col presidente non ci siamo mai tirati indietro. Abbiamo dovuto rispettare dei parametri. Nessuno ci ha vietato di vendere o comprare, semplicemente non ci siamo riusciti. A gennaio ci faremo trovare pronti. Le idee chiare le avevamo anche prima, nell’anno post scudetto abbiamo anche fatto 12-13 acquisti. Poi, è chiaro, c’è sempre qualcuno che esplode e chi meno. Cacciamani? Spesso si spendono cifre folli per chi non ha ancora dimostrato nulla. Dobbiamo stare attenti. Stiamo seguendo diversi giocatori. Il panorama italiano è ricco, ci sono giocatori interessanti, vogliamo dare loro opportunità. Guardiamo a tutti i campionati. Spesso escono diversi nomi, alcuni fuorvianti. Che giochi in Spagna, Francia o Inghilterra, l’innesto che ci servirà deve dare una mano. Ripeto, però: dobbiamo prima arrivare a gennaio! Varela? E’ un buon giocatore, ma attualmente abbiamo Hojlund, Lucca e Giovane che può essere impiegato nel ruolo di centravanti. Il portoghese sta performando, è difficile che il Monza si privi di un giocatore così. Se lo dovesse fare, non lo regalerà di certo. Il Napoli, in questo momento, non ha fatto alcun passo con nessuno”.

La Nazionale Polacca in Nations League è riuscita a racimolare 4 punti finora, è terza nella classifica del girone B. In questa pausa affronterà, sabato 14 novembre la trasferta in Romania e poi la Svezia in casa a Breslavia.

Secondo quanto arriva dalla Polonia, Przemysław Frankowski, Marcel Reguła e Piotr Zieliński non hanno preso parte all'allenamento di oggi. "Il primo dei sta lottando con un infortunio muscolare, mentre gli altri due hanno risentito degli effetti delle basse temperature e hanno preso il raffreddore. Al momento non è ancora noto se ci saranno o no nella gara contro la Romania", si legge. Un'influenza quindi alla base dello stop momentaneo del centrocampista dell'Inter. Nei giorni scorsi Thuram e Stankovic sono dovuti rientrare a Milano per problemi muscolari e hanno dovuto rinunciare alla Nazionale.
